answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, any disruption from onboarding a new primary vendor (memory_c2's cost win) carries outsized delivery risk in a 14-day window—exactly the scenario the objective warns against. Renewing without change leaves the 18% mandate unaddressed, and deferral isn't viable since the contract doesn't auto-renew. Negotiating with the incumbent (memory_c4, reinforced by c1's stability record and c6's volume-pricing precedent) offers a path to real cost reduction while preserving the proven integration and delivery continuity, avoiding the switching risk entirely. I want to verify memory_c4's archived record before committing, since the summary is vague on the magnitude of margin recovered and I need to know whether prior negotiations came close to an 18%-scale cut or something much smaller, which would change whether negotiation alone can satisfy finance's mandate or must be paired with a second-source move next cycle. Only one memory was consolidated per direction, so all of this is thin evidence—single-cycle outcomes, not repeated validation—so I'm treating the cost-target sufficiency of negotiation as uncertain and flagging that a fallback (partial vendor split) may be needed next review if the negotiated terms fall short.
